spec.title: User applications on native macOS (PROP-059) — source build, launchers, proxies, shell, external volume

p.purpose: **Purpose.** macOS has no Linux fixture coverage for: the parent-shell detection through `proc_pidpath` (zsh is the default login shell), the `/bin/zsh` fallback, a source build with the Xcode command-line tools, signals through the proxy in Terminal, and an external volume under `/Volumes` as a storage library. The owner proves these here, on a real Mac (`PROP-059#acceptance`).

p.isolation-note: Every step runs against an isolated settings root (`VIBE_SETTINGS`). The Vim source tarball (about 20 MB) is downloaded once and cached under that root.

facts.PRE-HOST: macOS 14 or newer on Apple silicon or Intel; Xcode command-line tools (`xcode-select --install`) for `cc`, `make` and the curses headers; network access to github.com.
facts.PRE-PACKAGE: The Vim bridge `org.vibevm.apps/vim@1.1.0` resolvable from the registry or from a checkout laid out as `<reg>/org.vibevm.apps/vim/v1.1.0/` with `--registry <reg>`.
facts.PRE-VOLUME: Optional for step 6: an external volume (USB disk or a mounted disk image) with a free directory.

section.title: Steps

facts.STEP-1-DETECT: **Detection picks the macOS source build for this CPU.**

p.EXP-1: **Expected.** `Detected: macos/aarch64` (or `x86_64`), the macOS platform listed first and marked detected, with exactly one installer detected for the CPU (`macos-source-arm64` or `macos-source-intel`, type `source_build`, one URL source, recipe `recipes/build-posix.sh`).

p.EXP-2: **Expected.** The tarball is fetched and verified, `configure` / `make` / `make install` output streams live, the install finishes in a few minutes, and the payload holds `bin/vim` (the wrapper), `bin/vim-bin` and `share/vim/vim92`. The tarball sits in `cache/app-sources/<sha256>/v9.2.1167.tar.gz`; `cache/app-build` is empty or absent (the work directory is deleted after success). `opt/bin/vim` is a copy of the proxy.

p.EXP-3: **Expected.** The banner says 9.2 with patches 1-1167. Inside Vim, `$VIMRUNTIME` is `…/opt/apps/vim/org.vibevm.apps.vim@1.1.0/share/vim/vim92` (not a path under `cache/app-build`), syntax highlighting works on a `.sh` file, and `:q` returns to the shell with exit 0.

section.fence: "$VIBE_SETTINGS/opt/bin/vim" # interactive: press Ctrl+C, then :q "$VIBE_SETTINGS/opt/bin/vim" & sleep 1; kill -TERM $!; wait $!; echo "exit=$?"

p.EXP-4: **Expected.** `Ctrl+C` reaches Vim, which shows its usual hint and keeps running; `:q` exits 0. `SIGTERM` to the proxy is forwarded to Vim and the proxy exits with `143` (128 + 15).

facts.STEP-5-SHELL: **`vibe shell` from zsh, from bash, and from an unrecognised parent.**

section.fence: $vibe shell # from the default zsh echo "$0 ${PATH%%:*}"; vim --version | head -1; exit bash -c "$vibe shell" # from bash python3 -c "import os; os.execv('$vibe', ['vibe', 'shell'])" # unrecognised parent

p.EXP-5: **Expected.** From zsh the child is the same zsh image; from bash it is that bash; from the Python parent it is the fallback `/bin/zsh`. In every case the first PATH entry is `$VIBE_SETTINGS/opt/bin`, `vim --version` works, and `exit` returns the shell's status. `--json` and a non-terminal invocation are refused.

facts.STEP-6-VOLUME: **An external volume as a library.** With a volume mounted at `/Volumes/USB`:

section.fence: $vibe storage add /Volumes/USB/vibe-apps --id usb $vibe storage move org.vibevm.apps/vim@1.1.0 --to usb vim --version | head -1 diskutil unmount /Volumes/USB $vibe app list; "$VIBE_SETTINGS/opt/bin/vim" --version; echo "exit=$?" # remount the volume $vibe app list $vibe storage move org.vibevm.apps/vim@1.1.0 --to default; $vibe storage gc

p.EXP-6: **Expected.** The library marker is written on the volume, the move copies the payload there (the wrapper keeps working because `$VIM` follows the payload), and `vim --version` runs from the volume. After unmounting, `app list` shows `unavailable` with the reason and the proxy exits 127 with one `vibe-app-proxy: unavailable: …` line. After remounting it is `ready` again without any command; the move back and `gc` leave nothing unreferenced.

facts.STEP-7-OFFLINE: **Offline reinstall from the source cache, then uninstall.**

p.EXP-7: **Expected.** The offline reinstall rebuilds from the cached tarball without network and replaces the payload in place. The uninstall deletes the payload directory and, as the last provider, the `opt/bin/vim` proxy; `opt/apps/vim` is empty.

facts.STEP-REQUIREMENT: **The MinGW requirement seen from macOS (PROP-065 `#app-dependencies`).** The Vim bridge's `windows-source` option requires `org.vibevm.apps/mingw-w64@^15.2` on its build step. A requirement is installed on the host that runs the installation, so on macOS it is described and refused, never installed.

section.fence: "$vibe" app describe org.vibevm.apps/vim --json | jq '.options[] | select(.id == "windows-source") | .steps[] | select(.requires) | {id, requires}' "$vibe" app plan org.vibevm.apps/vim --platform windows --arch x86_64 --installer windows-source --json; echo "exit $?"

p.EXP-REQUIREMENT: **Expected.** `describe` names the build step with `requires: [{package: "org.vibevm.apps/mingw-w64@^15.2", scope: "build"}]` without resolving anything. The plan is refused before any download with exit 2 and the error code `requirement_unresolved`, naming `org.vibevm.apps/mingw-w64@^15.2` and the absence of an installer option for this host; `$VIBE_SETTINGS` gains no `applications/index.json`.

p.pass-criteria: Every step reads as described on a real Mac: detection, the source build with the Xcode tools, the relocated runtime, signals through the proxy, `vibe shell` for zsh, bash and the fallback, the external-volume library with unavailability and moves, the offline rebuild and a clean uninstall. The owner signs the date below.

facts.EVIDENCE-2026-10-31: **Automated run of 2026-10-31 on `flash` (macOS 15.7 Intel, vibe `50a6685cc`, local registry copy, isolated `VIBE_SETTINGS`).** The `macos-source-intel` option built and installed Vim 9.2.1167 in 52 s and `opt/bin/vim --version` printed the banner; a second run with `--hidden` left `opt/bin` empty while `app list` showed the hidden installation; `vibe shell -g --with org.vibevm.apps/vim` in a real terminal (driven by `expect`) ran `vim --version` from the hidden installation; `app expose` wrote the proxy and made it the slot default; `storage move` to `~/opt/vibe-apps-final` kept the installation ready; `outdated` reported it current; `uninstall --plan-only` printed proxies, payload and record actions and `uninstall` left `opt/bin` empty. Signals, the shells and the external volume remain the owner's manual steps.
